reviewed_invariants: Each of the four cohort routes reproduces its exact frozen exporter annotations and separately reconciled metadata; a candidate cannot substitute newer producer status or invented samples.
Preview binds all three original and prepared target digests and the intended future apply path. Apply installs catalog, language metadata and normalization history in one guarded journal.
Installed inode intent is recorded before atomic rename. Rollback tracks intended restored inodes, handling an interruption immediately after either rename without losing ownership evidence.

Rollback attempts every still-owned target, preserves externally replaced or changed bytes, removes owned success receipts, and retains recovery payloads when an external conflict prevents restoration.
The common evidence lease remains held through final input pins, owned output identity/bytes, catalog identity/bytes, normalization-history replay and the repeated consumer-pin check.
Catalog snapshots reject direct and parent symlink redirection. Existing history absence remains distinct from an existing empty registry.

APL publication binds the separate approved static-runtime receipt and all repository input references within the held context, checks eleven exact candidate/original source/runtime/command/environment identities, and requires every declared runtime/proof pin among physically verified inherited evidence.
The original APL candidate false metadata-review flags remain unchanged; its later scope approval is a distinct publication audit reference.
Success is printed only after context exit; late closure failures invoke rollback before lease release.
fixed_finding: The original draft recorded an installed inode only after rename; intent-before-rename plus explicit restoration bookkeeping closes that interruption gap.
